measures.what_it_does: Replaces Dixie School District's capital levy, which expires at the end of 2026, with a six-year levy for 2027 through 2032 to keep funding health, safety and energy-efficiency repairs at Dixie School. Supporters say it would pay to shore up the building's foundation and level the gym floor. The same levy failed by one vote (107-108) in February 2026.
measures.cost_line: $75,000 a year for 2027 through 2032 ($450,000 in all), an estimated $0.50 per $1,000 of assessed value.
measures.pro_summary: The statement for, by Lisa and Dean Davis, says it 'does not create a new tax' because it replaces an expiring levy, that it would fix the settled gym floor and foundation, and that past levy projects (playground, sprinklers, dry wells, insulation) show the board is 'fiscally responsible with your tax dollars.'
measures.con_summary: No statement against was printed in the pamphlet; VoteWA's guide names Peter Berg as the committee against but carries no argument. The levy failed by one vote in February.

taxes.basis: A yes vote continues an excess property tax of about $0.50 per $1,000 for six more years. It replaces an expiring capital levy rather than raising a rate, so it maps at the renewal tier (+1).

measures.sources_note: Walla Walla County local voters' pamphlet pp. 22-23 (S1); VoteWA guide record 7378 (S2); sample ballot (S3); Union-Bulletin coverage of the February 2026 vote and recount (S4, S5) and of the general ballot (S6). The prior levy's rate was not found.

measures.what_it_does: Authorizes a one-year excess property tax for the Prescott Joint Park and Recreation District's maintenance and operation in 2027, its main source of operating money, chiefly for the Prescott community pool. The district covers parts of Walla Walla and Columbia counties and asks for this levy every year; the November 2025 request failed with 59.5% of the vote (60% needed).
measures.cost_line: $175,000 collected in 2027, approximately $0.35 per $1,000 of assessed value (about $70 a year on a $200,000 home, by the Union-Bulletin's 2025 estimate at the same rate).
measures.pro_summary: The statement for, by Hailey Hudson and Debby Phillips, says the pool is where kids learn to swim and teenagers find summer jobs, that families drove to other towns this summer without it, and that 'once a community pool is gone, it's incredibly difficult to bring it back.'
measures.con_summary: No statement against was submitted and no opposition committee was named. In November 2025, 40.5% of Walla Walla County voters in the district voted no on the same amount.

taxes.basis: A yes vote imposes a $175,000 excess levy (about $0.35 per $1,000) for 2027. After the 2025 levy failed, no excess levy is in place to renew, so approval restarts the tax at the amount voters rejected in 2025, above the $145,000 last approved.

measures.sources_note: Walla Walla County local voters' pamphlet pp. 24-25 (S1); VoteWA guide record 7379 (S2); sample ballot (S3); Union-Bulletin coverage of the 2025 levy, its early results and the certified failure (S4-S6). Columbia County's share of the 2025 vote was not found.
